questions.question_text: A company with an average net profit of Rs 30 crore over the last three years sets aside Rs 40 lakh for CSR in the current year. Under the Companies Act, 2013, the firm has:
options: Spent more than the required amount and may carry forward the excess

questions.question_text: A listed company contributes to a political party under its CSR budget. Under Schedule VII, such an expenditure is:
options: Eligible if the board of directors approves it
Eligible if the party works for social welfare
Not eligible to be counted as CSR expenditure
Eligible only up to 25% of the CSR budget

questions.question_text: A garment firm discloses a known fabric defect to the dealers although this reduces its sales. This is best explained as:
options: Poor management, as it harms the interests of the owners
Legal compulsion with no ethical content behind the decision
Ethical conduct, giving honesty priority over short-term profit

questions.question_text: An employee reports to a regulator that her company is dumping waste illegally. Her action is called:
options: Insubordination, which is always a breach of the contract
Whistle-blowing, which exposes wrongdoing from the inside
Industrial espionage, which sells secrets to competitors
Lobbying, which seeks favours from the government

questions.question_text: The "triple bottom line" evaluates a firm on:

options: Franchising, as it licenses its brand to a foreign partner
Outsourcing, as it is handed over to a local contractor
Offshoring, as the activity is relocated abroad
Insourcing, as it brings the activity back in-house

questions.question_text: A firm hands over its payroll processing to an outside agency in the same city. This is:
options: Backward integration, as it acquires a supplier
Outsourcing, as a function is passed to an outside agency
Divestment, as it sells a business unit

questions.question_text: An Indian company buys 60% of a Vietnamese factory and controls its management. This is:

questions.question_text: A café chain lets an entrepreneur use its brand and operating system in return for a fee and royalty. The entrepreneur is a:

Bureaucratic control, with quality as a rule-bound job

options: Outsourcing based on a vendor contract
Incremental innovation based on an old business model

Tax benefits, easier compliance and support for funding
Exemption from all the laws of the country

Manual bookkeeping of the daily sales

Higher rent for the office premises

options: Represent the promoter family on the board of directors
Represent the employees in the board meetings

options: Suppliers who sell to the company
Customers who buy from the company

Return any product after use without giving a reason to the seller
